policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV attaches the participle to the ship, not to the travellers: 'a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail unto the places on the coast of Asia'. The dative singular μέλλοντι agrees with πλοίῳ and yields that relative clause; the nominative plural μέλλοντες would make 'we' the ones intending to sail, which the ASV does not say.

ASV 'to sail unto the places on the coast of Asia' renders either the prepositional εἰς τοὺς ... τόπους or the bare accusative of goal after πλεῖν; English 'unto' is required in both cases and no note is mapped here.

Dative πορευθέντι agreeing with the implied 'him' of ἐπιτρέψας versus accusative πορευθέντα as subject of the infinitive; both give ASV 'gave him leave to go unto his friends and refresh himself'. The only note is a greek_gloss on 'receive attention', which concerns wording, not the case of the participle.
ἑκατοντάρχης and ἑκατόνταρχος are alternative declensions of the same noun; ASV 'the centurion' renders either and no note is mapped.
Word order of ἦν and πόλις only; ASV 'nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea' follows English order and cannot register the Greek sequence.

Λασαία and Λασέα are spelling variants of one place name, both conventionally anglicised 'Lasea'; the ASV form is the traditional English spelling and does not track either Greek vowel. No note is mapped.
Order of μᾶλλον and ἐπείθετο only; ASV 'gave more heed to the master' renders both orders identically.
Presence or absence of the article τοῦ before Παύλου; ASV 'than to those things which were spoken by Paul' shows no article on a proper name either way.

κἀκεῖθεν is crasis of καὶ ἐκεῖθεν; ASV 'advised to put to sea from thence' renders the adverb, and the connective καί is routinely left untranslated inside a clause already opened by 'And because the haven was not commodious'. The verse's only note is a greek_gloss on the wind names.
ASV transliterates 'Euraquilo', which reproduces Εὐρακύλων (Euro-aquilo); Εὐροκλύδων would give 'Euroclydon', the older English form the ASV declined to print.

ASV text reads 'a small island called Cauda' (Καῦδα), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read Clauda' places Κλαύδην in the margin — the note names the rejected reading, so the text is the base.
Order of ἰσχύσαμεν and μόλις only; ASV 'we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat' renders both orders alike, and the verse's textual note concerns the island's name, not this sequence.

ASV reads 'the third day they cast out with their own hands', a third person plural; ἐρρίψαμεν would require 'we cast out', which the ASV does not print despite the surrounding 'we' narrative. The only note is an alternative_rendering on 'furniture' and does not bear on the verb.
Order of ἐλπὶς and πᾶσα only; ASV 'all hope that we should be saved was now taken away' fixes English order and distinguishes neither.
Connective τε versus δέ; ASV opens 'And when they had been long without food', which renders either particle, and no note is mapped.

This unit and v018 are the two halves of one transposition: RP places ἄγγελος immediately after νυκτί, the base after τοῦ θεοῦ's clause. ASV 'there stood by me this night an angel of the God whose I am' names the angel once in English order and cannot show where the Greek noun stood.
Addition of the emphatic pronoun ἐγώ after εἰμι; ASV 'whose I am' supplies the ordinary subject pronoun that English requires with or without it, so the emphasis is invisible.
Counterpart of v016: ἄγγελος is present in the verse on every reading, only in a different position. ASV 'an angel of the God whose I am' is compatible with both placements.

μή που κατὰ τραχεῖς τόπους versus μήπως εἰς τραχεῖς τόπους: the negative particles are equivalent ('lest haply') and both κατά and εἰς with ἐκπίπτειν give ASV 'cast ashore on rocky ground'. The verse's note is an alternative_rendering on 'prayed'.
Order of ἀγκύρας and μελλόντων only; ASV 'as though they would lay out anchors from the foreship' renders both.
Order of ἀπέκοψαν and οἱ στρατιῶται only; ASV 'Then the soldiers cut away the ropes' places subject before verb as English requires, whichever Greek order stood.
Order of ἡμέρα and ἤμελλεν only; ASV 'while the day was coming on' renders both.
μεταλαβεῖν and προσλαβεῖν τροφῆς both yield 'to take some food'; the ASV wording matches either compound and no note is mapped.
ἀπό versus ἐκ before τῆς κεφαλῆς; ASV 'from the head of any of you' renders either preposition.
ASV reads 'there shall not a hair perish from the head of any of you'. 'Perish' renders ἀπολεῖται; πεσεῖται would give 'fall from the head', the wording the ASV does not print.
εἴπας and εἰπών are alternative aorist participle forms of the same verb; ASV 'when he had said this' renders either.

Order of the prepositional phrase ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ relative to αἱ πᾶσαι ψυχαί; ASV 'we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls' contains both elements and fixes their English order independently.

ASV gives the total as 'two hundred threescore and sixteen souls' = 276, which requires διακόσιαι. The WH reading ὡς would yield 'about seventy and six', both an approximation and a different number, and the ASV prints neither.
Presence or absence of the article τῆς with τροφῆς; ASV 'when they had eaten enough' does not render the noun's determination at all.
Imperfect ἐβουλεύοντο versus aorist ἐβουλεύσαντο; ASV 'they took counsel' is a simple past that renders either aspect. The verse's textual note bears on ἐξῶσαι/ἐκσῶσαι (v032), not on this verb.

ASV reads 'they took counsel whether they could drive the ship upon it' — a personal optative with the sailors as subject, which is εἰ δύναιντο. The impersonal δυνατόν would give 'whether it were possible to drive the ship', without the 'they could' the ASV prints.

ASV text reads 'drive the ship upon it' (ἐξῶσαι), and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read bring the ship safe to shore' consigns ἐκσῶσαι to the margin — the note names the reading not adopted.
ἐπέκειλαν and ἐπώκειλαν are alternative aorist forms for running a vessel aground; ASV 'they ran the vessel aground' renders either.
ASV reads 'by the violence of the waves'. The genitive τῶν κυμάτων is present in the English; the bare βίας would give only 'by the violence', with no 'of the waves' to render.
ἑκατοντάρχης and ἑκατόνταρχος are alternative declensions of one noun; ASV 'the centurion' renders either, as at 27:6 (v004).
